newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's Cabinet approves $300 mln Eurobond issue.
newsitem.headline: Panama's Cabinet approves $300 mln Eurobond issue.

text.p: Panama's Cabinet approved late Wednesday night the issue of up to $300 million in Eurobonds, a high-ranking government official said.

The funds would be used to help pay off the nation's external debt and the government is working out the details of the type of debt management plan, the official said, adding Bank of Boston will act as agent. He gave no further details.
Panama completed its Brady bond external debt restructuring package last year by issuing bonds for exchange of $3.5 billion of medium- and long-term commercial debt.
The bonds will be targetted to the European markets, and will not be sold in the U.S., a market source said.

The decision to issue Eurobonds came close on the heels on rate assignments from both Moody's Investors Services and Standard & Poor's Corp. Moody's assigned Panama Brady bonds a Ba1 rating, while S&P gave them a BB-plus. The ratings are among the highest in Latin America.
